response.why: batch: player A starts

Keep. 2 lands + early removal (Anoint) + two flying creatures (Faerie Mastermind, Spyglass Siren) for the clock. Island untaps for turn-1 blue plays. This is exactly the shape of hand the mirror wants: interaction + evasive clock. The deck plays plenty of flash creatures, so sequencing is flexible.

Darkslick Shores is the best play—it's a flexible mana source (taps for {U} or {B}, enters untapped on turn 1) that sets up turns 2+ better than a monocolored Island. Playing a land on turn 1 is essential for mana development in this control mirror; passing cedes tempo and is suboptimal. Darkslick Shores > Island > Pass.

Cast Spyglass Siren. Turn 1 with only one land, passing just delays mana development—I'd be sitting idle while the opponent makes their next move. Casting Spyglass Siren establishes the flying clock (fliers are the real race in this mirror) and generates a Map token, giving me intrinsic value even if the creature is later removed. The creature has summoning sickness but can block. Taking the initiative here is better than reactive stalling with no concrete play.

Pass priority. Upkeep with no triggers; standard progression to draw step. I'm ahead on board (Spyglass Siren established while opponent has only a Swamp), so I'll draw and evaluate my main phase plays.
Pass. Draw phase complete; proceed to precombat main phase where I'll evaluate casting Preacher of the Schism (2/4 deathtouch, {2}{B}) or other threats now that I have three lands available.

Play Island is the best play. By turn 3, I've only developed one land (Darkslick Shores) and no Islands yet, so playing an Island now is essential mana development. It enables bigger plays next turn (e.g., Preacher of the Schism {2}{B}) and standard early-game progression. Passing is passive and slow. Sacrificing the Map Token for card selection is okay but less efficient than developing mana when my mana base is still thin.

Cast Faerie Mastermind (65) or Floodpits Drowner (63) to establish more flying threats—fliers are the real clock in this mirror. Faerie Mastermind edges it out because it triggers on opponent draws for card advantage (mirrors the draw-penalty aspect of Sheoldred). Floodpits Drowner is also strong with vigilance for attack/block flexibility. Pass (50) is control-play passive. Sacrificing Map Token (48) for card selection is slower. Anoint with Affliction (15) has no legal target on the current board, making it a wasted spell and mana.

Attack with Spyglass Siren. Establishing the clock is essential in the mirror—a flying 1/1 that can't be blocked by ground creatures is exactly the evasive threat that wins long games. Spyglass Siren taps, but Faerie Mastermind (2/1) provides defense against flying creatures the opponent is likely to play next turn. The 1 damage matters in the race, and I'm taking the initiative rather than playing passively. Passing (48) cedes tempo and waits for the opponent to establish their own clock.

Cast Floodpits Drowner (65). Adding a third flying creature to my board establishes a dominant clock—I'll have three flying creatures (Siren, Mastermind, Drowner) to the opponent's one Faerie Mastermind (which has summoning sickness). Floodpits Drowner has flash and vigilance, giving flexibility for defense while maintaining offense. This is the aggressive play needed to press my advantage in the mirror. Passing (48) is passive and lets the opponent make a move. Casting Anoint with Affliction (20) either gets countered or results in a bad board state based on the leaf—worse than passing.

Play Undercity Sewers (60). It develops your mana base while providing surveil 1, which filters your deck for answers in the control mirror. Though it enters tapped (same as Island for immediate untapped land count next turn), the surveil benefit gives card selection—finding Preacher of the Schism, removal, or other threats. Playing Island (55) is solid mana development but lacks the filtering. Passing (45) is passive; with all your lands tapped, you gain nothing by holding back.

Attack-all (68): Deal 3 damage (Spyglass Siren 1 + Faerie Mastermind 2) and reduce opponent to 16 life. Floodpits Drowner has summoning sickness so can't attack. This maintains aggressive clock pressure—in the mirror, being the beatdown is key. Both your flying creatures tap, but the opponent's Faerie Mastermind is also tapped and summoning sick, so they have limited threats next turn. Hold[Spyglass Siren] (55) is safer but only deals 2 damage. Hold[Faerie Mastermind] (50) deals just 1 damage. No attack (40) concedes all momentum.

Pass (60). Your board is strong with three flying creatures (Siren, Mastermind, Drowner) and all mana untapped. The opponent's Preacher of the Schism has summoning sickness, so it's not an immediate threat—it can't attack yet. Casting Anoint with Affliction (35) appears to remove your own Faerie Mastermind instead of the opponent's threat (based on the leaf state showing your Mastermind gone but Preacher still present), making it a bad trade. Hold your board together and see what the opponent does next turn.

Pass priority. Upkeep with no triggered abilities to respond to. Casting Anoint with Affliction now is tactically wrong—the previous leaf_eval showed it results in losing your Faerie Mastermind (based on the board state after casting). Better to hold your removal for a more critical moment, or cast it during your main phase when you can evaluate threats more carefully. Pass and move to draw step.

Pass (58). Keep your board intact with all three flying creatures (Siren, Mastermind, Drowner) and untapped mana going into your main phase. The opponent's Preacher of the Schism has summoning sickness, so it's not an immediate threat. Casting Anoint with Affliction (30) results in losing your Faerie Mastermind based on the previous leaf state analysis, while Preacher remains on board—a losing trade. Better to hold your removal and evaluate threats during your main phase.

Pass priority. Same situation as the draw step evaluation—casting Anoint with Affliction results in losing your Faerie Mastermind for no clear benefit (the opponent's Preacher remains on board). Better to proceed to your main phase with all creatures intact and full mana available to evaluate your options (playing a land, casting Preacher of the Schism, or holding up removal).

Cast Preacher of the Schism (70) is the best play. It establishes a strong threat (2/4 deathtouch) on the board alongside your fliers. Deathtouch is crucial here—it means your Preacher kills any creature that blocks it, controlling the opponent's board. Having two Preachers in play (yours and theirs) creates a complex board state that favors your tempo. Playing Island or Swamp (52) is solid mana development but doesn't create threats. Sacrificing Map Token (54) upgrades Mastermind to 3/2, but casting Preacher is better for establishing control. Casting Anoint with Affliction (20) still results in losing your Faerie Mastermind. Pass (48) is passive.

Play Island or Swamp (both 60). After casting Preacher, you have four creatures on board (strong position) but all three lands are tapped. Playing a land develops your mana base for future turns—next turn you'll untap and have more resources to work with. Island and Swamp are equally valuable here, both adding generic mana for future plays (removal, creature casting, etc.). Passing (52) leaves your board strong but doesn't prepare for the turns ahead; mana development is important in the mid-game.

Sacrifice Map Token (60) to upgrade Preacher of the Schism to 3/5. The boost is significant—from 2/4 to 3/5 makes Preacher much harder for the opponent to kill or block effectively (especially with deathtouch). In the control mirror, a more powerful creature is better than keeping 1 untapped mana open. You already have Anoint with Affliction as flexible removal if needed. Passing (54) preserves flexibility but leaves your Preacher at 2/4, which is weaker against the opponent's threats.

Target Preacher of the Schism (index 2). It's already your strongest creature (2/4 with deathtouch), and making it 3/5 maximizes the value of the explore effect. Whether you hit a land (gains time) or a non-land (+1/+1 boost), Preacher benefits the most. Upgrading a 2/4 deathtouch creature to 3/5 creates a devastating blocker and attacker that's much harder for the opponent to deal with.

Attack-all (Siren + Mastermind + Drowner = 5 damage unblocked, 3 blocked; opponent 11 or 13). You've established a strong board (upgraded 3/5 Preacher, multiple fliers) and should press your advantage. Holding back creatures is too passive—you're the beatdown here with 4 untapped creatures vs opponent's 2 (one tapped, one with summoning sickness). Unblocked deals 5 damage and leaves Drowner untapped for future plays. Even if blocked for 3 damage, that's solid progress from 16 life toward the win.

No-blocks. You're ahead on the board (Preacher clock still active and untapped), life totals are healthy (16 is safe), and opponent is already at 13 after your attack. Blocking with your Preacher trades away your best threat and gains only 2 life—not worth it when you should be closing the game. Keep the Preacher untapped to attack again next turn and maintain pressure on your 13-life opponent.

Pass. You're in a winning position: 16 vs 13 life, with a strong, untapped board (Siren + Mastermind fliers + Preacher clock). The opponent's Sheoldred is summoning sick and is your main threat once it activates on turn 10. Your plan: attack for 3 damage/turn and close by turn 13, before Sheoldred becomes a problem. Casting Anoint removes your Preacher (shown in leaf 1), sacrificing your best blocker against Sheoldred. Drawing both players a card doesn't advance your position and costs 4 mana. Hold everything and attack next turn to maintain tempo.

Casting Anoint with Affliction loses your Preacher (shown in Decision 24 leaf 1), sacrificing your best defensive wall and clock piece. You're in a winning position with strong board control and don't need to burn resources.

Cast Enduring Curiosity. You drew it this turn and it's a powerhouse: 4/3 creature with flash, triggers card draw when your creatures deal combat damage, and recursively returns as an enchantment when it dies. Combined with your Siren (1), Mastermind (2), and Preacher (3), you have 10 damage on turn 10—reducing the opponent from 13 to 3 in one attack. That closes the game by turn 11. Passing is solid but passive. Casting Anoint removes your Preacher (bad). Drawing is neutral. The upside of a card draw engine + fat threat far outweighs spending your 4 mana now.

Play Swamp. Both lines result in the same combat (attacking with Siren, Mastermind, Preacher for 6 damage, reducing opponent to 7 life), but playing your land gives you 1 untapped mana next turn (5 lands vs 4). In a control mirror where you're closing the game, extra mana flexibility is valuable for responding to opponent plays or casting additional threats. Playing a land is free; there's no downside to deploying it now.

This keeps your momentum going toward closing the game.
